title: UJUR: A Hardware Jitter-Based Seed-Free Synthetic Data Generator for Python
abstract: ujur is an open-source Python library for generating synthetic datasets without deterministic seeds. Entropy is sourced from consecutive nanosecond timestamps via the OS hardware-backed monotonic clock (perf_counter_ns), with stride sampling and modulo extraction (t mod 1000). The method produces near-uniform distributions over {0,...,999} and passes all 15 NIST SP 800-22 statistical randomness tests. The library provides a numpy-style API for uniform, normal, and correlated data generation, regression datasets with user-specified parameters, and snapshot-based persistence instead of seeds. Zero external dependencies.

title: Construction of the standards system for safety and emergency mannagement in highway reconstruction and expansion projects based on knowledge graph
abstract: The standards system for safety and emergency management in highway reconstruction and expansion projects provides an important institutional and technical basis for construction safety management. A well-structured standards system can clarify the scope of safety management and identify priorities for the development and revision of relevant standards, thereby supporting technological progress in the industry. However, conventional approaches to standards-system construction rely heavily on expert judgment and domain knowledge, and usually involve qualitative procedures such as document collection, status investigation, and expert workshops. As a result, the construction process may be subjective and insufficiently data-driven. With the increasing accumulation of textual data from highway reconstruction and expansion projects, knowledge graph techniques offer a new approach to extracting structured knowledge from unstructured engineering documents. In this study, an unstructured-text-mining-based knowledge graph method is proposed. The method uses the ERNIE pre-trained language model to encode unstructured texts, applies a BiLSTM model with an attention mechanism for named entity recognition, and introduces a CRF layer to model label dependencies and obtain optimal sequence labels. The extracted entities and semantic relations are then organized into a knowledge graph to support the construction of a standards system for safety and emergency management. Compared with BERT-BiLSTM and BiLSTM-CRF models, the proposed ERNIE-BiLSTM-ATT-CRF model improves the F1 score by approximately 4.0% and 6.8%, respectively, with more evident advantages under small-sample conditions.

title: Zero-Shot Image Classification in Low-Resource Medical Image Diagnosis Using Fine-Tuning Transformer Models
abstract: Deep learning-based (DL) medical picture identification frequently relies on huge annotated datasets, which are hard to come by in actual clinical settings. Significant domain mismatch prevents transformer-based vision-language models from being directly applied to medical imaging, despite their strong zero-shot performance on natural images. This paper analyzes the usage of pre-trained vision–language transformers for brain MRI tumor classification under zero-shot and low-resource scenarios and highlights the limits of direct zero-shot inference and prompt-based adaptation. To address these issues, a lightweight few-shot adaptation technique based on partial unfreezing of the vision transformer is developed, enabling selective domain-specific learning while keeping pre-trained knowledge. The suggested technique considerably improves classification performance utilizing only 20 labeled samples per class, beating both zero-shot and frozen few-shot baselines. These findings suggest that in clinical settings with limited annotation, minimum and regulated transformer fine-tuning offers an efficient and data-efficient method for brain MRI categorization.

title: All Eyes on the Workflow: Automated and Efficient Event Discovery from Video Streams
authors: Wil M. P. van der Aalst
abstract: Disciplines such as business process management and process mining aid organizations by discovering insights about processes on the basis of recorded event data. However, an obstacle to process analysis is data multi-modality: for instance, data in video form are not directly interpretable as events. Existing approaches rely on a dictionary of activity label as input, cannot provide frame-by-frame labeling explanations, or rely on superseded computer vision techniques. In this work, we present SnapLog, an approach to extract event data from videos by converting frames to feature vectors using image embeddings and performing temporal segmentation through frame-wise similarity matrices. A generalized few-shot classification is then used to assign labels to the video segments, yielding labeled, timestamped sub-sequences of frames that are interpretable as events. Conventional process mining techniques can be used to analyze the resulting data. We show that our approach produces logs that accurately reflect the process in the videos.

title: Placing and routing quantum LDPC codes in multilayer superconducting hardware
abstract: Abstract Quantum error-correcting codes with asymptotically lower overheads than the surface code require nonlocal connectivity. Leveraging multilayer routing and long-range coupling capabilities in superconducting qubit hardware, we develop Hardware-Aware Layout, HAL: a robust, runtime-efficient heuristic algorithm that automates and optimizes the placement and routing of arbitrary codes. Using HAL, we generate around 150 explicit layouts of quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes. We study codes with topological structure and find that removing the periodic boundaries significantly lowers the hardware complexity with only a moderate reduction of logical efficiency. We also lay out highly nonlocal qLDPC code families that achieve competitive tradeoffs between hardware complexity and logical efficiency. Based on our findings, we anticipate many novel qLDPC codes to be realizable on near-term superconducting qubit hardware and inform future directions for the co-design of quantum devices and fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Prévision de la ressource solaire intrajournalière à partir de méthodes d'apprentissage profond appliquées à des images de satellites météorologiques géostationnaires
abstract: Integrating photovoltaic generation into the power grid is challenging because of the variability oft he solar resource. Intraday forecasts, from a few minutes to a few hours ahead, contribute to grid balancing,the optimization of self-consumption, and energy trading. At these lead times, geostationary satellites provide direct observations of the evolution of cloud cover over a given area, but traditional forecasting techniques have certain limitations. This thesis first investigates deterministic deep-learning approaches that produce a single future trajectory from a short history of satellite cloud images. The second part proposes a generative approach based on diffusion and flow-matching models, capable of producing several plausible futures cenarios from the same observations, thereby providing information about forecast uncertainty and representing a broader range of complex cloud evolutions and fine-scale structures, such as convection, multilayer cloud configurations, and cloud formation and dissipation. Finally, the choice of deep-learning architectures is discussed in light of different operational requirements.

title: Asymptotics of Effective Regularization and Overfitting Regimes in Kernel Ridge Regression with Power-Law Spectra
abstract: Modern machine learning has witnessed a striking empirical phenomenon: overparame terized neural networks, trained to perfectly interpolate noisy training data, often generalize remarkably well, defying classical statistical intuition that such interpolation should lead to overfitting. Understanding this behavior is one of the relevant and interesting challenges in learning theory. Afruitful approach has been to study kernel ridge regression (KRR). In the infinite-width limit, training a neural network with gradient descent corresponds to kernel regression with the neural tangent kernel (NTK). Building on recent works that derived convenient closed form expressions for the expected test risk of KRR in terms of the kernel eigenspectrum, we perform an asymptotic analysis for the case of decaying ridge parameter and the exact power-law spectra and the spectra majorized by a power law. We discuss the assumptions underlying these closed-form expressions and indicate how they can be relaxed to more realistic settings, following the narrative of the relevant works in this direction. Our main results characterize the asymptotic behavior of the effective regularization parameter and the noise overfitting coefficient (which determines the test risk for pure noise). We find that the relative decay rates of the ridge parameter and the kernel eigenvalues governs the overfitting regime. We then connect these results to the effective dimension of the input domain (the support of the data distribution) with respect to the kernel, introduced by Takhanov [14] via Kolmogorov n-widths. This provides a link between the intrinsic dimension of the data (as seen through the kernel) and the type of overfitting. We also obtain upper bounds for spectra majorized by a power law and discuss open problems for further work.

title: Applications of Claude AI in Healthcare, Education, and Customer Support
abstract: This research paper explores the applications of Claude AI, a large language model, across key sectors including healthcare, education, and customer support. The study examines how artificial intelligence can enhance efficiency, automate routine tasks, and improve decision-making processes in real-world environments. In healthcare, Claude AI assists in medical documentation, symptom analysis, and patient communication. In education, it supports personalized learning, tutoring, and content generation. In customer support, it enables automated responses, chatbot systems, and customer interaction management. The paper highlights the benefits, challenges, and ethical considerations associated with deploying AI-based conversational systems. It also discusses future opportunities for integrating artificial intelligence into digital transformation initiatives across industries.

title: ECM²RS: Explainable Causal Multi-Modal Reasoning System
abstract: Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence have enabled the development of multimodal systems capable of reasoning over both visual and textual data. Visual Question Answering (VQA) is a key application in this domain; however, most existing models operate as black-box systems, lacking transparency and interpretability. Additionally, these systems often suffer from language bias, leading to unreliable and non-generalizable predictions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes ECM²RS (Explainable Causal Multi-Modal Reasoning System), a novel framework that integrates multimodal deep learning with neuro-symbolic reasoning and explainability techniques. The system leverages LLaVA as the core reasoning engine and incorporates multi-level explanation modules, including visual explanations using gradient-based methods, textual explanations via attention mechanisms, and knowledge-based reasoning from external datasets. The proposed approach is evaluated using VQA, CLEVR, and ScienceQA datasets to ensure both real-world applicability and logical reasoning capability. Experimental results demonstrate that ECM²RS enhances interpretability while reducing black-box behaviour, producing coherent and explainable reasoning outputs. This work contributes toward building trustworthy and interpretable multimodal AI systems

title: Research on the development of an automated system for psychology questionnaire generation based on large language models
abstract: This study reimagined the psychology questionnaire development process using large language model ((LLM) technology, aiming to overcome the protracted preparation cycles and significant human bias inherent in traditional scale development. We developed a specialized fine-tuning scheme for a corpus of 169 professional psychological questionnaires. By integrating instruction fine-tuning with human feedback reinforcement, we significantly enhanced the adaptability of the Qwen-2.5 and GLM-4 models for demanding professional psychological assessment tasks. The optimized models demonstrated remarkable gains across key dimensions: text generation quality (BLEU-4 increased by 0.05, ROUGE-L by 0.057), scientific rigor (logical consistency improved by 28.6%), and cultural adaptability (achieving over 85% accuracy in cross-regional expression conversion). This research solidly supports the feasibility of leveraging LLM technology to drive research paradigm transformation in psychology, offering crucial methodological support for developing efficient, intelligent psychological measurement tools.

title: Optimizing Multi‑Agent Collaborative Architectures with OpenClaw: A Gateway‑Driven Approach for Practical Training Environments
abstract: With the rapid advancement of large language models, multi agent systems are increasingly deployed in educational contexts, yet they often suffer from inefficient task scheduling and inconsistent automated evaluation. This paper presents an optimized multi agent architecture based on the OpenClaw framework, tailored for railway signaling practical training. The architecture employs a Gateway orchestrated priority scheduling mechanism that segregates high concurrency simple queries from compute intensive evaluation tasks, coupled with a five dimensional automated scoring pipeline integrated with Feishu Base and DeepSeek V3.2. A one click cloud deployment on the Feishu platform was implemented and evaluated with 86 students. Results show that the proposed system achieves a Pearson correlation of 0.89 with instructor scores, reduces average response latency by 63.5%. Furthermore, teaching effectiveness metrics indicate a 13.7% improvement in theory scores, a 70.4% reduction in grading time, and high learner satisfaction.

title: EduSense: Advancing Teaching with Audio-Visual Analytics
abstract: In the recent years examining the specific manner by which teaching will influence learning, and it happens that the mechanisms most often used to check it (such as grade surveys, the occasional peer review) are rather biased and slow. EduSense is a novel AI-based installation that attempts to provide a more objective perspective because in real-time it constantly monitors facial expressions and the body angle in relation to each other. It integrates the best computer vision features (YOLOv8 to detect objects, MediaPipe to pose-track, DeepFace to detect face vibes, audio: Whisper to transcribe and OpenSMILE to tone. Detection of emotions and tracking of postures allow EduSense to record it all, such as the level of teacher emotions to his or her sitting position, indicating us not only with the presence of attention, but also with the body language in the mix. The system achieves 4 step pipeline and finally scores 89.4% on emotion recognition on seven emotions and 94 percent on posture orientation on four directions. These are comparatively high numbers in accordance with student feedback (r = 0.74) and even provide time stamp granularity that can be used to frame future instructional adjustments. In essence, it demonstrates how multimodal sensing would make the existing spot-and-comment format a derivative of data, as a continuous loop, and this is in line with UN SDG 4 and 9.

title: Representational Harms in LLM-Generated Narratives Against Global Majority Nationalities
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for text generation tasks from everyday use to high-stakes enterprise and government applications, including simulated interviews with asylum seekers. While many works highlight the new potential applications of LLMs, there are risks of LLMs encoding and perpetuating harmful biases about non-dominant communities across the globe. To better evaluate and mitigate such harms, more research examining how LLMs portray diverse individuals is needed. In this work, we study how national origin identities are portrayed by widely-adopted LLMs in response to open-ended narrative generation prompts. Our findings demonstrate the presence of persistent representational harms by national origin, including harmful stereotypes, erasure, and one-dimensional portrayals of Global Majority identities. Minoritized national identities are simultaneously underrepresented in power-neutral stories and overrepresented in subordinated character portrayals, which are over fifty times more likely to appear than dominant portrayals. The degree of harm is amplified when US nationality cues (e.g., ``American'') are present in input prompts. Notably, we find that the harms we identify cannot be explained away via sycophancy, as US-centric biases persist even when replacing US nationality cues with non-US national identities in the prompts. Based on our findings, we call for further exploration of cultural harms in LLMs through methodologies that center Global Majority perspectives and challenge the uncritical adoption of US-based LLMs for the classification, surveillance, and misrepresentation of the majority of our planet.

Notably, we find that the harms we identify cannot be explained away via sycophancy, as US-centric biases persist even when replacing US nationality cues with non-US national identities in the prompts. Based on our findings, we call for further exploration of cultural harms in LLMs through methodologies that center Global Majority perspectives and challenge the uncritical adoption of US-based LLMs for the classification, surveillance, and misrepresentation of the majority of our planet.

title: Enhancing Large Language Models for Identifying and Prioritizing Important Medical Jargons From Electronic Health Record Notes Using Data Augmentation: Comparative Study
abstract: Background OpenNotes allows patients to access their electronic health record (EHR) notes through online patient portals. However, EHR notes contain abundant medical jargon, which can be difficult for patients to comprehend. One way to improve comprehension is by reducing information overload and helping patients focus on the medical terms that matter most to them. Objective This study aimed to evaluate both closed-source and open-source large language models (LLMs) for extracting and prioritizing medical jargon from EHR notes relevant to individual patients, leveraging prompting techniques, fine-tuning, and data augmentation. Methods We evaluated the performance of closed-source and open-source LLMs on a dataset of 90 expert-annotated EHR notes. We tested various combinations of settings, including (1) general and structured prompts, (2) zero-shot and few-shot prompting, (3) fine-tuning, and (4) data augmentation. To enhance the extraction and prioritization capabilities of open-source models in low-resource settings, we applied data augmentation using GPT-4o and integrated a ranking technique to refine the training process. Additionally, to measure the impact of dataset size, we fine-tuned the models by incrementally increasing the size of the augmented dataset from 10 to 9995 and tested their performance. The effectiveness of the models was assessed using 10-fold cross-validation, providing a comprehensive evaluation across various settings. We report the F1-score and mean reciprocal rank for performance evaluation using two different string matching algorithms (relaxed string matching and Jaccard Index). We also conducted an error analysis classifying the erroneous outputs from the models. Results Our results show that open-source models achieved the highest performance, particularly when using fine-tuning with a gold-standard dataset. Under Jaccard Index–based string matching, DeepSeek 8B set the benchmarks with an F1-score of 0.431 (SD 0.046); similarly, BioMistral 7B showed a mean reciprocal rank of 0.577 (SD 0.109). However, under relaxed string matching, open-source models were unable to match the performance of closed-source models, even with data augmentation or fine-tuning. We analyzed our experiment from several perspectives. First, few-shot prompting did not show an advantage over zero-shot prompting in vanilla models. Second, when comparing general and structured prompts, we found that model performance could deviate largely based on prompting styles. Third, fine-tuning with a small gold-standard dataset improved performance. Finally, data augmentation yielded performance comparable to or even surpassing the fine-tuning strategy. However, it also underscored the importance of the quality of the augmented dataset. Conclusions The evaluation of both closed-source and open-source LLMs highlighted the effectiveness of prompting strategies, fine-tuning, and data augmentation in enhancing model performance in low-resource scenarios.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Its Applications in Quantum Computing: A New Frontier in Information Processing
abstract: Quantum entanglement, where two or more particles become correlated in such a way that the state of one particle is dependent on the state of the other(s), regardless of the distance between them, is an important concept in quantum mechanics. Here, we explore the role of quantum entanglement in quantum computing, by looking at its basic principles, and the new levels of processing power and security it allows. We also discuss the latest advances, problems and opportunities of quantum entanglement in information processing technologies, such as quantum algorithms, quantum encryption and its effect on conventional computers.

title: The Challenge of Code-Switching: Sentiment Analysis in Multilingual Social Media Data
authors: Sumedh Gajbhiye, Himangshu Mistry, Akhil Kamble, Shahil Barsagade, Kashyap Ramteke, Ayaz Shaikh
abstract: This an important study as it tackles the issue of parsing huge amounts of informal, unstructured user-generated content on X and Instagram. The proposed work designs a solid pipeline for polarity classification by using supervised machine learning framework using Sentiment140 and Hinglish_Sentiment datasets. The project includes novel preprocessing and cleaning methods for social media-specific, shorthand slangs, and text that is limited by a certain number of characters. Early results show that sentiment detection can be done with a high degree of accuracy, confirmed our belief that this type of automated analysis is precise and scalable; an essential component in real-time market research, public policy tracking and helping clients navigate community mood.

title: Configuration-Aware Natural Gradient Optimization for Variational Quantum Circuits
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) are commonly developed under the assumption that a parameterized circuit corresponds to a single, well-defined physical realization. In practice, this assumption is not satisfied. Differences in compilation, gate ordering, and hardware-level perturbations lead to multiple admissible circuit realizations, each associated with a distinct objective over the same parameter space. The resulting optimization problem is therefore not defined by a single loss function, but by a family of configuration-dependent objectives whose aggregate behaviour must be considered. This study formulates optimization explicitly at the level of such configuration families. A consistent extension of natural-gradient methods is developed in which both the descent direction and the local geometric structure are obtained through averaging across configurations. The resulting update preserves the structure of quantum natural gradient methods while ensuring alignment with the family-defined objective. The approach is evaluated using exact statevector simulations on transverse-field Ising and Heisenberg Hamiltonians under controlled variability. Across all tested regimes, the method produces lower average loss, substantially reduced dispersion across configurations, and improved worst-case performance relative to both configuration-specific optimization and gradient-averaged baselines. These results show that when the objective depends on a set of admissible circuit realizations, optimization must be constructed at the same level to obtain stable and reliable solutions.

title: Unlocking the Power of Lifelong Learning
abstract: In an era marked by the rapid growth of big data and high-performance computing, machine learning (ML) has seen unprecedented expansion. This increase in data availability and advancements in computational power have opened new avenues for solving complex tasks. However, a significant challenge remains: datasets often exist in isolation, limiting the potential insights that can be derived from integrating multiple data sources. Moreover, ML algorithms frequently perform asymmetrically with varying data volumes. To overcome these challenges, the AI community is developing lifelong machine learning (LML), a paradigm that mirrors human incremental learning. LML systems continuously acquire knowledge and adapt to different tasks, promising enhanced flexibility, adaptability, and intelligence. This article provides a comprehensive overview of LML techniques and methodologies, highlighting the limitations of traditional static learning approaches.

title: A Natural Language Full-Scenario Multimodal Conversion Method and System for Enterprise-Level Analysis
abstract: Traditional natural language parsing solutions for enterprise digital transformation face critical limitations: narrow scenario coverage (confined to single tasks like NL2SQL), low semantic parsing accuracy (≤75% for non-standard terminology in professional fields), and poor scalability due to tightly coupled architectures. These flaws fail to meet demands for cross-system collaboration, real-time analysis, and multi-round dialogue continuity. This paper proposes a full-scenario multimodal conversion method with a seven-step closed-loop framework. It integrates BGE-M3 embedding and Milvus vector retrieval for intent classification across four core business scenarios, adopts a BiLSTM-based context understanding engine with attention mechanism to resolve multi-round dialogue context loss, and designs a loosely coupled, hot-swappable modular conversion engine. A microservice-based enterprise-level system is developed. Experimental verification in State Grid scenarios shows outstanding performance: intent classification accuracy 96.3%, non-standard terminology parsing accuracy 95.7%, multi-round intent recognition accuracy ≥98%, cross-system instruction execution success rate 99.5%, and cross-scenario operation efficiency improved by 82%. Non-technical personnel onboarding time is ≤1 hour. The system features strong compatibility, scalability, and practicality, applicable to power, finance, and manufacturing industries, providing a novel solution for enterprise-level natural language intelligent interaction and cross-system data collaboration.

title: A parallel hybrid architecture integrating transformer and convolutional neural network for tabular classification
abstract: Tabular data is widely present in various real-world application scenarios. While Gradient Boosting Decision Tree(GBDT) models have long dominated this field, they are limited by their lack of end-to-end learning capabilities and difficulty in modeling complex feature interactions. Although deep learning approaches have emerged, they often suffer from high computational costs and training instability. To address these challenges, we propose PTformer, a novel parallel hybrid architecture. By integrating a Transformer encoder with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) branch, PTformer synergizes the capture of global long-range dependencies via self-attention with the extraction of local feature correlations using 1D convolutions. This fusion yields enriched feature representations. Extensive experiments on five public datasets, ranging from small to large-scale benchmarks, demonstrate that PTformer consistently outperforms mainstream tree models (such as XGBoost, LightGBM) and deep learning baselines (TabNet, FT-Transformer) in Accuracy, Precision, and F1-Score. Notably, the model exhibits significant performance advantages on large-scale datasets. Furthermore, efficiency analysis reveals that PTformer achieves a single-sample inference latency of approximately 1 ms while maintaining competitive training speeds, offering an efficient and robust solution for modern tabular data modeling.

title: Human centric conversational system in Tamil using Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Living in rural and under-resourced communities, people are frequently relying on the use of simple telephone as there is a low access to the internet and low smartphone rates. Traditional Interactive Voice Response systems are menu-based, rigid and not very conducive to natural speech in local languages. This paper proposes an artificial intelligence-based bilingual voice-first application that translates Tamil and English while talking using a regular GSM phone. The design that is proposed combines multi-language speech recognition, generative text that is retrieval augmented, natural language understanding, and neural text-to-speech synthesis as part of a flexible telephony platform that can be configured to operate with little or no network connectivity. Local audio routing based GSM call simulation layer is used to eliminate the expensive third-party telephony APIs and minimize the cost of testing and deployment. Experimental assessments reveal a high degree of cross-accent speech recognition, appropriate response generation, and use as a result of conversations, as well as a high level of user-satisfaction. It provides the telephonic services with the much-needed accessibility increase and creates a feasible platform on which voice automation can be easily scaled in such areas like education, healthcare, customer care, and delivery of public services.

title: Interpretable Automated Feature Engineering: A Comprehensive Review with a Focus on Dynamic and Stationary Environments
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive review of Automated Feature Engineering (AFE) methods, with a focus on their application in static data environments and explores recent advancements in dynamic Feature Engineering (FE) for evolving data contexts. AFE is essential in modern Machine Learning (ML) pipelines, as it addresses the drawbacks of traditional FE, which often relies heavily on domain expertise and is labor intensive. By automating this process, AFE has the potential to enhance the efficiency, performance, and interpretability of ML workflows. The paper analyzes the methods, strengths, and limitations of different AFE methods. The review also identifies critical research gaps and proposes directions for future advancements. This work serves as a foundational resource for researchers aiming to optimize ML performance through novel AFE strategies.

title: MTServe: Efficient Serving for Generative Recommendation Models with Hierarchical Caches
abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) offers superior modeling capabilities but suffers from prohibitive inference costs due to the repeated encoding of long user histories. While cross-request Key-Value (KV) cache reuse presents a significant optimization opportunity, the massive scale of individual user states creates a storage explosion that far exceeds physical GPU limits. We propose MTServe, a hierarchical cache management system that virtualizes GPU memory by leveraging host RAM as a scalable backup store. To bridge the I/O gap between tiers, MTServe introduces a suite of system-level optimizations, including a hybrid storage layout, an asynchronous data transfer pipeline, and a locality-driven replacement policy. On both public and production datasets, MTServe delivers up to 3.1* speedup while maintaining near-perfect hit ratios (>98.5%).

title: Adaptive Algorithm Selector Meta-learning
abstract: Abstract Opting the most applicable machine learning algorithm for a dataset is a complex and time- consuming task. Different algorithms perform else depending on the structural parcels of the dataset. The No Free Lunch Theorem shows that no one algorithm can do better than all others for every possible problem. Thus, intelligent model selection mechanisms are needed to reduce homemade trial and computational cost. This paper proposes an Adaptive Algorithm Chooser (AAS) based on Meta-Learning. The system studies past learning gests and dataset characteristics to recommend the most suitable algorithm for new datasets. The proposed frame includes dataset characterization, meta- point birth, meta-database construction, meta-model training, and intelligent recommendation. Experimental evaluation shows that the adaptive chooser improves effectiveness and reduces trial-and-error sweats compared to traditional approaches. Keywords — Adaptive learning, Algorithm Selection, AutoML, Adaptive Systems, Model Recommendation

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Creative Entity: Legal Standards, Copyright Limitations, and Emerging Frameworks for Authorship
abstract: Artificial Intelligence now is far beyond the scope of the first application as the device that helps humans. The existing AI has the power to compose music, draw, compose stories, create videos, create architecture and even compose computer code. The legal question, which this development raises, is: Who is the author of an AI-generated work? The copyright laws in India were fashioned in a way that could only allow human beings to produce works of creativity. With AI being a significant component of the creativity process, the issues of ownership, rights, and legal protection arise. The notion that humans are the only potential authors provides loopholes in a great majority of jurisdictions, providing that AI-generated works do not fall under the current copyright laws.

title: Hierarchical Predictive Intelligence (HPI):Support-Induced Ternary Projection
abstract: This paper introduces the Hierarchical Predictive Intelligence (HPI) framework—a theoretical blueprint for autonomous agents capable of scientific discovery. We unify latent predictive world modeling (JEPA) with rigid symbolic inference. The core mechanism is the transition from continuous representations to discrete structures via non-invertible coarse-graining operators and Brusentsov’s ternary logic. We define epistemic lacunae as structural voids in the world model that trigger the formation of structured knowledge. Finally, we prove the asymptotic consistency of the conflict resolution operator based on the Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle under identifiability and coverage constraints.

title: Classified Adverts Collection
abstract: The dataset contains 355 classified advertisements organized into 15 semantic categories and represented as structured JSON objects for supervised multi-class text classification. Each advertisement includes a unique identifier, category identifier and title, advertisement title, full advertisement text, and an LLM-assisted summary. The accompanying category data provide category identifiers and titles together with category-level bag-of-words (BOW) and TF-IDF representations derived from the advertisement corpus. The corpus consists predominantly of Ukrainian-language advertisements and includes naturally occurring mixed Ukrainian–Russian content. The texts preserve characteristics of real-world advertisements, including spelling variations, colloquial language, repetitions, commercial information, and stylistic variability. The dataset covers multiple thematic domains, including furniture, commercial premises and rentals, cosmetics, perfumery, healthcare and beauty products and services, medical products, and equipment. The dataset is intended for research and educational purposes and can be used for supervised text classification, evaluation and benchmarking of machine learning and large language model (LLM)-based classifiers, natural language processing research, feature engineering, and comparative evaluation of text classification methods.

title: Behavioral Drift Analytics for Preventive Fraud Risk Management in Digital Financial Platforms
abstract: The rapid expansion of digital platforms and online financial ecosystems has substantially increased vulnerabilities to fraudulent activities, account takeovers, and anomalous user behaviors. Traditional risk detection methodologies operate reactively, identi- fying threats only after financial losses or security breaches have materialized. This paper presents the Behavioral Drift Analytics Early Warning System (BDA-EWS), a novel predictive analytics framework specifically architected to detect gradual, cumula- tive changes in user behavior before they culminate in adverse events. The system establishes personalized behavioral baselines through comprehensive statistical profiling of historical transaction data. Unlike conventional anomaly detection approaches that focus on point anomalies, BDA-EWS employs adaptive sliding window analysis with temporal decay to continuously monitor for subtle, evolving shifts in behavioral patterns over time. We introduce a novel multi-component Behavioral Drift Score (BDS) that integrates marginal drift measurements, Mahalanobis distance for multivariate correlation analysis, and Jensen-Shannon di- vergence for distributional change quantification. The framework prioritizes algorithmic transparency through integrated feature contribution analysis, enabling identification of specific behavioral attributes driving detected drift. Extensive evaluation on the enhanced PaySim-2026 dataset comprising 6,362,620 transactions demonstrates that BDA-EWS provides risk alerts 3–7 days before fraudulent transactions with a false positive rate of 8–12%, significantly outperforming point-anomaly methods (25–35% FPR) while maintaining competitive detection accuracy (F1-score: 0.87–0.92). These results establish behavioral drift analytics as an effective paradigm for preventive risk management in contemporary digital financial environments.

title: Using the SISSO Machine Learning Algorithm to Optimize Physics Course Teaching
abstract: In modern education, integrating machine learning techniques into college physics courses not only enhances students' interest in learning but also improves teaching quality. The SISSO (Sure Independence Screening and Sparsifying Operator) algorithm, as an efficient data-driven method, has been proven to have significant advantages in verifying and deriving physical formulas. This paper explores the application of the SISSO algorithm in college physics teaching and aims to demonstrate its potential to improve teaching efficiency and students' understanding for physics and machine learning through practical case studies.

title: An Experimental Analysis of Data Augmentation and Pretraining for Mammogram Image Classification
abstract: Breast cancer continues to be one of the major health challenges for women worldwide and detecting it at an early stage greatly increases the chances of successful treatment. Mammography remains the standard imaging technique for identifying tumors at their earliest development. In this study, an attempt is made to classify mammogram images as benign or malignant by applying deep learning-based methods. The MIAS dataset is used for model training, while the larger CBIS-DDSM dataset serves as a source for pretraining to strengthen feature learning. Since MIAS contains a limited number of images, several augmentation and preprocessing techniques—such as rotations, horizontal and vertical flips, Gaussian blurring, CLAHE contrast adjustment, and median filtering—are incorporated to enrich the dataset and improve image quality. Two backbone architectures, ResNet18 and ResNet50, are examined for the classification task. The experiments indicate that ResNet18, when paired with MoCo-based pretraining and the enhanced augmentation pipeline, reaches a validation accuracy of about 65%. In contrast, the same model without these improvements performs noticeably lower at around 52%. The study highlights that effective preprocessing and representation-learning strategies can substantially enhance model performance, even when only a small amount of annotated medical data is available.

title: Relaxation-Informed Training of Neural Network Surrogate Models
abstract: ReLU neural networks trained as surrogate models can be embedded exactly in mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs), enabling global optimization over the learned function. The tractability of the resulting MILP depends on structural properties of the network, i.e., the number of binary variables in associated formulations and the tightness of the continuous LP relaxation. These properties are determined during training, yet standard training objectives (prediction loss with classical weight regularization) offer no mechanism to directly control them. This work studies training regularizers that directly target downstream MILP tractability. Specifically, we propose simple bound-based regularizers that penalize the big-M constants of MILP formulations and/or the number of unstable neurons. Moreover, we introduce an LP relaxation gap regularizer that explicitly penalizes the per-sample gap of the continuous relaxation at training points. We derive its associated gradient and provide an implementation from LP dual variables without custom automatic differentiation tools. We show that combining the above regularizers can approximate the full total derivative of the LP gap with respect to the network parameters, capturing both direct and indirect sensitivities. Experiments on non-convex benchmark functions and a two-stage stochastic programming problem with quantile neural network surrogates demonstrate that the proposed regularizers can reduce MILP solve times by up to four orders of magnitude relative to an unregularized baseline, while maintaining competitive surrogate model accuracy.

title: On the Hybrid Nature of ABPMS Process Frames and its Implications on Automated Process Discovery
abstract: A core component of any AI-Augmented Business Process Management System (ABPMS) is the process frame, which gives the system process-awareness and defines its maximal behavioral boundaries. Compared to traditional process models, the process frame should, in principle, provide a somewhat more permissive representation of the managed processes, such that the (semi) autonomous behavior of an ABPMS, referred to as framed autonomy, could emerge. In addition, the process frame is not limited to a single linguistic or symbolic formalism and may incorporate heterogeneous knowledge ranging from predefined procedures to common sense rules and best practices. In this paper, we first conceptualize the ABPMS process frame as a hybrid business process representation, consisting of semi-concurrently executed procedural and declarative process models, extending the open-world assumption of the declarative paradigm also to procedural models. The latter allows any set of (non-conflicting) models of either type to be combined for execution, but complicates the automated discovery of these models from event data. Existing approaches for procedural models are particularly affected due to their reliance on observing directly-follows relations between pairs of activities. In search of an alternative, we present an in-depth analysis of how different procedural behaviors manifest as sets of discovered Declare constraints, each corresponding to a specific type of eventually-follows relation. This reveals behavioral overlaps between declarative and procedural models, while also laying the foundation for developing corresponding process (frame) discovery techniques.

title: Semantics Map for TUS Triad v1
abstract: Abstract The Semantics Map for TUS Triad v1 defines the primitive-to-pointer grounding layer for TUS Triad receipt stacks. It specifies how semantic primitives exposed by canonical receipts and triad-level artefacts are grounded in concrete JSON Pointer paths, and it establishes the citation allowlist discipline that governs what may be cited in refs and meta_refs during downstream validation and reporting. The document is a mapping registry, not a writing rulebook, domain profile, or interpretive guide. It does not determine domain meaning, report posture, thresholds, labels, or narrative conclusions. Its role is narrower and more foundational: to define which emitted receipt and triad surfaces are admissible as grounding evidence for specific classes of claim, and which surfaces are identity-only, descriptive-only, or unavailable for semantic grounding. A central purpose of the map is to prevent interpretive overreach. MANIFEST surfaces are constrained to identity, file-binding, pairing, and joinability use in meta_refs; they do not become semantic grounding surfaces for refs. Audit renders, renderer echoes, convenience mirrors, and duplicated values are excluded unless explicitly allowlisted. LANDING receipt semantics are also separated into canonical field-response surfaces, realised first-step LANDING transition, and distinct continuation endpoint, preventing those surfaces from being collapsed into a single unsupported interpretation. The map also defines scope-prefix handling, wildcard and placeholder semantics, profile-bounded matching, pair-resolution rules, set-level grounding surfaces, and coordinate-system safeguards for rank-space and line-space claims. In v1, it deliberately withholds directional polarity licensing for Phi and delta_p_rank, preventing claims such as “more coherent,” “less ambiguous,” or equivalent directional readings unless a future map version explicitly provides the required primitive and grounding paths. Within the wider TUS OS® architecture, this document functions as a governance-layer specification. It supports independent validation, report conformance, and bounded interpretation by ensuring that claims remain tied to declared receipt and triad surfaces. It is intended to be used alongside the TUS Binding Manual, Core Rubric, Domain Profile, validator/checker configuration, and report templates. Included files Semantics Map for TUS Triad v1.pdf — Public v1 Semantics Map for TUS Triad, defining primitive-to-pointer grounding, artifact scopes, citation allowlist boundaries, refs / meta_refs separation, MANIFEST identity-only surfaces, LANDING first-step versus continuation semantics, set-level grounding surfaces, and coordinate-system safeguards. title: BU32 Why Godel, Tarski, Russell, and AI Alignment Share One Missing Layer
abstract: Abstract This paper argues that Gödel incompleteness, Tarski undefinability, Russell’s paradox, and the AI alignment problem are not four unrelated difficulties, but four stratified readouts of one missing layer: the absent permission layer. The central claim is that a formal or operational system becomes unstable when the object layer attempts to substitute for the standing-source of its own legitimacy. In such cases, writable items are misread as standing-bearing objects, formability is misread as object-formation license, executability is misread as admissible boundary authority, and internal derivability is misread as truth closure. On this basis, the paper introduces a structural distinction between the object layer and the permission layer. The object layer handles expression, manipulation, inference, and execution. The permission layer grants the admissibility of objecthood, semantic closure, truth settlement, formation standing, goal legitimacy, and boundary persistence. Once this distinction is made explicit, Gödel’s theorem is reclassified as a readout of missing truth permission, Tarski’s theorem as a readout of missing semantic permission, Russell’s paradox as a readout of missing formation permission, and AI alignment failure as a readout of missing goal–execution–boundary permission. The paper therefore relocates the common root of these problems from isolated technical limits to an upstream ontological absence: the failure to establish the grounding layer that authorizes closure in the first place.

title: Beyond the “Black Box”: How Explainable AI Promotes Consumer Forgiveness Through Perceived Control
abstract: This study proposes a computational framework for adaptive explanation generation in AI recommendation systems. The framework distinguishes three explanation modes—no explanation, information-based explanation, and interaction-based explanation—and selects the optimal mode based on a user control demand model. We operationalize the framework through a rule-based decision algorithm that considers recommendation failure severity and user feedback history. To evaluate its effectiveness, we conduct a single-factor three-level between-subjects experiment (N=143). Results show that the interaction-based explanation significantly enhances perceived control (β=0.7645, p<0.001) and fully mediates forgiveness (indirect effect=0.4926, 95% CI [0.2872,0.7256]), validating the framework's core assumption. This work contributes a design-time algorithm for explanation policy and empirical evidence for human-centric XAI.

title: Research on a New Basketball Teaching Model Based on Video Capture and Physiological Characteristics
abstract: Addressing the pain points of subjective evaluation, delayed feedback, and insufficient personalization in traditional basketball teaching, this study constructs an intelligent teaching model integrating multi-view video capture and physiological parameter analysis. Taking shooting teaching as an empirical scenario, the model acquires kinematic and physiological data through synchronous video capture via smartphones and wearable monitoring (heart rate, blood oxygen). Based on a dual-dimensional fuzzy comprehensive evaluation system of “motor skill-physiological function”, it realizes quantitative diagnosis of learners' status and identification of shortcomings. A total of 60 subjects were recruited (32 novices and 28 specialized students). The results show that: the evaluation system can effectively distinguish skill levels (a comprehensive mean difference of 21.1 points, P<0.001); the “skill-physiology” combined weakness diagnosis was recognized by 91.7% of the subjects (score ≥4 points); the dynamically generated personalized teaching plans achieved a high recognition rate of 86.7%. The average feedback time from data collection to report generation is 4.2±0.9 minutes. This study confirms that the model promotes the objectification of teaching evaluation, the immediacy of feedback, and the personalization of strategies, providing a low-cost and operable technical path for “sports-intelligence integration”. The study also discusses limitations regarding technical precision, physiological metric selection, sample size, and evaluation criteria, outlining directions for future research.

title: Cryptography-Based Secure Voting System for College Elections
abstract: The primary method used in universities to select student representatives is through an electoral process. A cryptographically safe voting technique created especially for this study presents the use of Homomorphic Encryption for campus elections because Fully Homomorphic Encryption can aggregate encrypted votes without requiring decryption; vote manipulation and illegal access can be prevented, thereby maintaining the system’s vulnerability and dependability. This technology increases the effectiveness and reliability of college elections by removing security threats and human counting problems. The proposed system is implemented using RLWE based Brakerski–Gentry–Vaikuntanathan(BGV) homomorphic encryption scheme, which allows computations on the encrypted data. Also, the user interface is designed for vote casting.

title: Introduction
abstract: This introduction explores the growing presence of offensive language on social media platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram, where anonymity often encourages more aggressive behaviour. It discusses the difficulty in distinguishing between what is ‘merely offensive’ and what crosses into illegal or grossly offensive territory, highlighting how this is a complex issue spanning multiple disciplines. The chapter highlights the importance of linguistic insights in understanding offensive language, especially given the limitations of automatic detection systems and the inherently subjective nature of offence. It also provides an overview of the chapters that follow.

title: Quantum Circuit Partitioning For Effective Utilization of Quantum Resources
abstract: Near-term hardware is constrained by high error rates, small qubit counts, and relatively low output fidelity, making the execution of large, high performance quantum circuits difficult. Circuit partitioning (or circuit cutting) has emerged as a promising approach to circumvent these limitations by decomposing circuits into smaller subcircuits at two-qubit interaction points. However, it remains unclear which classes of circuits benefit the most from partitioning and under what hardware conditions it is most effective. In this work, we evaluate the suitability of quantum circuits for partitioning from three perspectives: improving fidelity, enabling distributed execution, and scaling to larger circuit sizes. Specifically, we compare uncut circuit execution against two circuit partitioning approaches: Qiskit's automatic cut finding technique and a custom performance optimized circuit cutting method. We also measure these across GHZ, QFT, brickwork, and random quantum circuits ranging from 4 to 14 qubits, using mean absolute error of expectation values and overall output fidelity. Our results show that partitioning benefits larger, highly interconnected circuits, with our custom method reducing error by up to 55\% and improve fidelity for GHZ circuits, but degrading performance for brickwork circuits at larger scales.

Our results show that partitioning benefits larger, highly interconnected circuits, with our custom method reducing error by up to 55\% and improve fidelity for GHZ circuits, but degrading performance for brickwork circuits at larger scales.

title: Advances in quantum genetic algorithms
abstract: Quantum Genetic Algorithms (QGA) are an emerging field of multivariate quantum optimization that emulate Darwinian evolution and natural selection, with vast applications in chemistry and engineering. The appropriate application of fitness functions and fitness selection is the problem-encoding step and the slowest step in designing QGAs for specific physical applications. In this paper, we provide a comprehensive review of these crucial steps. Our survey maps cases of quantum advantage, classifies and illustrates QGAs and their subroutines, and discusses the two main physical problems tackled by QGAs: potential energy minimization of particles on a sphere and molecular eigensolving. We conclude that the encoding used by the Thomson problem is a decisive step toward the use of QGAs in a variety of physical applications, while Grover’s search as a selection step in Reduced QGAs is the main driver of speedup. Although the small scale of simulations and the emergent nature of QGA optimizations make their complexity analyses difficult, recent studies are focusing on strategies to scale QGAs up.

title: طراحی الگوی اجرای خطمشیگذاری هوشمند در سازمانهای عمومی با تاکید بر نقش آموزش
abstract: با توجه به چالش‌های پیچیده در مدیریت کلان و لزوم گذار از روش‌های سنتی به تصمیم‌گیری‌های داده‌محور، این تحقیق به دنبال شناسایی و تبیین روابط بین مؤلفه‌های اثرگذار بر اجرای هوشمند خط‌مشی‌هاست از این رو تحقیق حاضر با هدف، ارائه و اعتبارسنجی الگوی اجرای خط‌مشی‌گذاری با محوریت هوش مصنوعی در سازمان تأمین اجتماعی استان خوزستان است. این تحقیق از نظر روش تحقیق از حیث هدف، کاربردی و از نظر روش جمع‌آوری داده‌ها، در زمره پژوهش‌های توصیفی-پیمایشی قرار دارد. در فاز کمی، بر اساس شاخص‌های استخراج شده از مرحله کیفی، پرسشنامه‌ای محقق‌ساخته طراحی شد. جامعه آماری پژوهش شامل مدیران و کارشناسان ارشد سازمان تأمین اجتماعی استان خوزستان بود که با استفاده از فرمول کوکران، تعداد ۳۲۵ نفر به روش نمونه‌گیری تصادفی طبقه‌ای به عنوان نمونه انتخاب شدند. جهت تجزیه و تحلیل داده‌ها از روش مدل‌سازی معادلات ساختاری با نرم افزار SmartPLS3 و برای وزن‌دهی به عوامل از فرآیند تحلیل سلسله‌مراتبی استفاده شد.یافته‌های حاصل از تحلیل تحلیل سلسله مراتبی نشان داد که از میان ابعاد اصلی، «الزامات اخلاقی و حاکمیتی» با وزن (۰.۶۰۳) و «تحول و نوآوری سازمانی» با وزن (۰.۵۸۶) بالاترین اولویت را در موفقیت اجرای خط‌مشی هوشمند دارند. همچنین نتایج بخش مدل‌سازی ساختاری نشان داد که تمامی شاخص‌های برازش مدل (از جمله مقادیر t بالاتر از ۱.۹۶ و سطح معناداری کمتر از ۰.۰۱) مورد تأیید قرار گرفتند. نتایج حاکی از آن است که زیرساخت‌های فناوری، کیفیت داده‌ها و آمادگی نیروی انسانی تأثیر مثبت و معناداری بر پیاده‌سازی موفق الگوی خط‌مشی‌گذاری هوشمند دارند، در حالی که «کیفیت داده‌ها»

title: Benchmarking Empirical Privacy Protection for Adaptations of Large Language Models
abstract: Recent work has applied differential privacy (DP) to adapt large language models (LLMs) for sensitive applications, offering theoretical guarantees. However, its practical effectiveness remains unclear, partly due to LLM pretraining, where overlaps and interdependencies with adaptation data can undermine privacy despite DP efforts. To analyze this issue in practice, we investigate privacy risks under DP adaptations in LLMs using state-of-the-art attacks such as robust membership inference and canary data extraction. We benchmark these risks by systematically varying the adaptation data distribution, from exact overlaps with pretraining data, through in-distribution (IID) cases, to entirely out-of-distribution (OOD) examples. Additionally, we evaluate how different adaptation methods and different privacy regimes impact the vulnerability. Our results show that distribution shifts strongly influence privacy vulnerability: the closer the adaptation data is to the pretraining distribution, the higher the practical privacy risk at the same theoretical guarantee, even without direct data overlap. We find that parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, such as LoRA, achieve the highest empirical privacy protection for OOD data. Our benchmark identifies key factors for achieving practical privacy in DP LLM adaptation, providing actionable insights for deploying customized models in sensitive settings. Looking forward, we propose a structured framework for holistic privacy assessment beyond adaptation privacy to identify and evaluate risks across the full pretrain-adapt pipeline of LLMs.

title: Schema as an Interface for AI Agents
abstract: This technical report analyzes the shift in Schema.org utilization from a descriptive SEO tool to a functional interface for AI agents. As search ecosystems transition from indexing to autonomous intermediation, structured data becomes a critical interpretative layer for LLMs and agentic systems. The paper defines a framework for "Operational SEO," focusing on entity clarity, intent classification, and machine-readable actionability. By providing specific technical implementations and case studies, the research demonstrates how structured web architectures enable AI agents to move beyond content retrieval toward autonomous decision-making and task execution.

title: Cost-sensitive adaptive XGBoost algorithm for imbalanced data stream
abstract: To address the challenge that the coexistence of class imbalance and concept drift in data stream hinders the smooth execution of classification tasks, this study proposes an online ensemble algorithm integrating cost-sensitive learning—Cost Sensitive Adaptive XGBoost (CSAXGB). The algorithm incorporates a cost-sensitive method to guide the model to focus on minority classes, dynamically assigns weights to base classifiers based on the Area Under the Curve and the Matthews Correlation Coefficient, and ultimately generates prediction results through weighted voting. To verify the performance of CSAXGB, experiments were carried out on 3 synthetic datasets and 5 real-world streaming datasets. The results show that in the two evaluation indicators of kappa and G-mean, CSAXGB has the best comprehensive performance.

title: Causal AI for Next-Generation Computing: From Statistical Correlations to True Reasoning
abstract: The paradigm shifting of Causal AI denotes a shift in artificial intelligence by tranistion beyond correlation-based models to the causation driven based decision making. As in the traditional AI systems which highly depend on the statistical associations approaches, but in causal AI based approach it unfolds underlying cause and effect relations, which provides us with greater accuracy, higher interpretability and much robust decision making. In this paper we explores the various foundational principles related to causal AI, the methodologies which drive it by including models like counterfactual reasoning and Structural Causal Models (SCMs) along with its applica- tions through various diverse domains like finance, healthcare, autonomous systems, cyber security and other related areas. We also focused on the various key obstacles hindering in the overall adoption of the same like ethical concerns, data limitations and computational complexity. At last, we emphasize on the future research directions by including integrating deep learning with causal AI, enhanced scalability factor and improved interpretability as by placing causal AI as the next confiner in intelligent computing.

title: Hebbian inertia and massless reasoning: comparative cognitive architecture in human and large language model systems
abstract: Abstract Purpose Human societies and artificial intelligence models learn in fundamentally different ways. Humans update beliefs through repeated exposure, a Hebbian process that creates cognitive “inertia”: once reinforced through experience, beliefs resist change. Large language models (LLMs), by contrast, do not update their parameters at inference; they pivot instantly between perspectives, unburdened by cumulative experience. Despite growing interest in comparing human and machine cognition, no prior study has placed both on a shared measurement scale that permits direct quantitative comparison. This paper reports the first such comparison, examining whether the architectural differences between human and LLM cognition produce measurably distinct signatures in belief structure and change. Design/methodology/approach We employ the Galileo Method, a multidimensional scaling technique that derives spatial representations of concepts from paired-comparison judgments of dissimilarity. Unlike conventional approaches that impose Euclidean geometry on psychological data, the Galileo Method preserves measured distances in their native metric, allowing non-Euclidean structures to emerge when warranted by the data. Participants - both human respondents and three LLM systems (Claude, DeepSeek, and ChatGPT-5) - provided dissimilarity judgments for identical concept sets. These judgments were then projected into coordinate spaces, enabling comparison of distances, clustering patterns, and response to belief-challenging information across agent types. Findings Human respondents display inertial pseudo-Riemannian signatures consistent with Hebbian learning: concepts reinforced through experience occupy stable positions that resist perturbation. LLMs, by contrast, exhibit what we term “massless” reasoning dynamics, repositioning concepts fluidly without the friction imposed by prior reinforcement, all arrayed in Euclidean space. These patterns held across all three LLM systems tested, suggesting they reflect architectural properties of transformer-based models rather than idiosyncrasies of particular implementations. Research implications The results point toward a research program in comparative cognitive architecture. By placing human and machine cognition on shared measurement frameworks, researchers can move beyond impressionistic comparisons to systematic analysis of how different learning architectures shape the structure and malleability of belief. Originality/value This study provides the first direct human–LLM comparison using a shared, geometrically unconstrained measurement scale; demonstrates that Hebbian inertia leaves detectable signatures absent in LLM cognition; and establishes a methodological template for future comparative work.

title: Inter-Stance: A Dyadic Multimodal Corpus for Conversational Stance Analysis
abstract: Social interactions dominate our perceptions of the world and shape our daily behavior by attaching social meaning to acts as simple and spontaneous as gestures, facial expressions, voice, and speech. People mimic and otherwise respond to each other's postures, facial expressions, mannerisms, and other verbal and nonverbal behavior, and form appraisals or evaluations in the process. Yet, no publicly-available dataset includes multimodal recordings and self-report measures of multiple persons in social interaction. Dyadic recordings and annotation are lacking. We present a new data corpus of multimodal dyadic interaction (45 dyads, 90 persons) that includes synchronized multi-modality behavior (2D face video, 3D face geometry, thermal spectrum dynamics, voice and speech behavior, physiology (PPG, EDA, heart-rate, blood pressure, and respiration), and self-reported affect of all participants in a communicative interaction scenario. Two types of dyads are included: persons with shared past history and strangers. Annotations include social signals, agreement, disagreement, and neutral stance. With a potent emotion induction, these multimodal data will enable novel modeling of multimodal interpersonal behavior. We present extensive experiments to evaluate multimodal dyadic communication of dyads with and without interpersonal history, and their affect. This new database will make multimodal modeling of social interaction never possible before. The dataset includes 20TB of multimodal data to share with the research community.

title: A review of the evolution and challenges of few-shot medical image semantic segmentation
abstract: Image segmentation, as a fundamental task in computer vision, aims to achieve pixel-level delineation between target regions and background. In the field of medical image analysis, traditional segmentation methods heavily rely on large-scale, high-quality annotated datasets. However, expert-level annotations for medical images require substantial professional human resources ( e.g ., radiologists performing slice-by-slice delineation of lesions) and face challenges such as cross-institutional data heterogeneity. To address this data bottleneck, few-shot medical image semantic segmentation has emerged as a promising paradigm. By leveraging strategies such as meta-learning, metric learning, and other related approaches, these approaches enable models to accurately segment the target region and achieve effective generalization to novel categories using minimal annotated samples (typically ≤15 instances per class), thereby significantly reducing dependence on annotated data. This article systematically explores foundational concepts such as medical image segmentation methods, benchmark datasets, performance evaluation metrics, and main approaches for few-shot medical image segmentation. Distinct from existing review literature, our work focuses on summarizing prototype-based few-shot medical image semantic segmentation algorithms. We analyze network architectures from a problem-oriented perspective and critically examine limitations in current methodologies. Finally, grounded in our analysis of current challenges, we propose forward-looking perspectives for future advancements.

title: Adaptive Exploration Proximal Policy Optimization for Efficient Robotic Continuous Control
abstract: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) is widely adopted for robotic continuous control, yet it can suffer from insufficient exploration and unstable policy updates in high-dimensional action spaces. This paper proposes Adaptive Exploration Proximal Policy Optimization (AE-PPO), an enhanced PPO framework that integrates (i) adaptive clipping, which adjusts the clipping range according to the observed magnitude of policy updates to better balance stability and learning progress, (ii) adaptive entropy regularization, which schedules the entropy weight across training to maintain effective exploration while avoiding excessive randomness. AE-PPO is evaluated on standard MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks (e.g., Walker2d, HalfCheetah, and Humanoid) and compared with PPO and representative baselines such as Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) and Soft Actor Critic (SAC). The results show that AE-PPO achieves faster convergence and an improved final performance with reduced training variance, demonstrating more stable and efficient learning in challenging high-dimensional tasks.

AE-PPO is evaluated on standard MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks (e.g., Walker2d, HalfCheetah, and Humanoid) and compared with PPO and representative baselines such as Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) and Soft Actor Critic (SAC). The results show that AE-PPO achieves faster convergence and an improved final performance with reduced training variance, demonstrating more stable and efficient learning in challenging high-dimensional tasks.

title: Human vs. LLM-Generated Speech Transcripts: Psycholinguistic Proxies and Discourse Dynamics
abstract: Voice cloning enables realistic fake speech in which a speaker’s identity is preserved while the spoken message is semantically altered. This paper asks whether such meaning-level manipulation leaves detectable traces in transcripts alone. To study this problem, we introduce FakeSpeech+, a paired real–fake dataset built from authentic speech clips and their matched semantically altered counterparts, re-embedded into cloned voices while preserving speaker identity. Using this dataset, we conduct a transcript-first analysis based on interpretable text-only features from two groups: (i) linguistic content organization and discourse dynamics, and (ii) compact production-related proxy cues, including hesitation and disfluency markers. We evaluate these cues under transcript-length control through residualization and compare authentic and manipulated transcripts using statistical and experimental analyses. The results show that only a limited subset of features retains strong separation after length control, with coordination-related structure and emotion anchoring emerging as the clearest cues, while several production-related and discourse-variability features show weaker but still informative differences. In contrast, a number of syntactic, lexical-diversity, and other discourse-level features show substantial overlap after residualization. These findings indicate that transcript-level structure and selected production-related cues remain informative under realistic content-manipulation threats, supporting the value of transcript-based analysis for identity-preserving fake speech.

title: Construction and Application of Computer Vision Virtual Teaching and Research Room under the Background of Intelligent Education
abstract: Under the background of the deep integration of intelligent education and industrial digitalization, computer vision, as a core direction of artificial intelligence, is facing prominent problems in talent training, such as scattered and lowly updated teaching and research resources, insufficient industry-university collaboration, and limited cross-university and cross-regional cooperation. Taking the teaching and research reform of computer vision as the starting point, this paper constructs a trinity virtual teaching and research room system featuring in-depth industry-university collaboration, efficient cross-university linkage, and interactive teacher-student co-creation. It integrates generative artificial intelligence, virtual simulation, digital twin and other intelligent technologies to form a new teaching and research model of mechanism reconstruction + technology empowerment + teaching and research practice. The practice was carried out among 120 teachers and 600 students from 8 universities. An evaluation system was established from three dimensions: teaching and research resource construction, teaching practice effect and industrial talent adaptability. The results show that the virtual teaching and research room increases the sharing rate of high-quality teaching and research resources by 42.3%, speeds up resource update by 2.3 times, improves students' core technical ability by 15.7%∼18.2%, raises algorithm implementation efficiency by 48.6%, and enhances talent industrial adaptability by 39.5%. This model effectively solves the bottlenecks of traditional teaching and research rooms in resources, collaboration and practice, and provides a replicable and promotable path for the construction and application of virtual teaching and research rooms for engineering majors under the background of intelligent education.

title: Optimizing LLM-based EFL Writing Assistants: A Social-Emotional Adaptive Scaffolding Framework Driven by Multi-dimensional User Profiling
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing; yet, today's generative tools remain largely blind to learners’ socio-emotional needs—a gap that risks turning AI into a cognitive crutch, especially for students with lower self-efficacy. Our analysis of 308 students from Chinese private universities reveals a prevalent preference for linguistic refinement (70.13%) over full-text generation (13.31%), as well as notable gender and disciplinary variations in patterns of AI dependency. To enhance human-AI interaction, we propose the Social-Emotional Adaptive Scaffolding (SEAS) framework, a modular four-layer structure designed to map multi-dimensional users’ attributes to dynamic feedback strategies. By translating pedagogical insights into technical logic, SEAS employs adaptive prompt engineering to deliver customized interventions—ranging from Socratic inquiry for high-proficiency learners to affectively resonant feedback for high-anxiety cohorts. This research establishes a foundation guided by user needs for developing future human-centered writing aids, emphasizing the integration of Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) within technical systems to reduce dependency and promote learner autonomy in the age of generative AI.

title: Multi-Agent Interaction: Creating Websites with Ease
abstract: Website development is traditionally a complex and time-consuming process requiring specialized skills across various domains such as design, coding, content management, SEO, and deployment. This paper presents a novel approach to simplify and automate the process through the use of multi agent systems (MAS), where intelligent, autonomous agents collaborate to handle different aspects of website creation. Each agent is specialized—for example, in UI/UX design, backend development, database configuration, or search engine optimization—and works in coordination with others to fulfill user-defined requirements. Leveraging principles of distributed artificial intelligence, these agents communicate, negotiate tasks, and make real-time decisions to generate complete, responsive, and optimized websites with minimal human intervention. The system incorporates natural language interfaces for ease of use, allowing even non-technical users to describe their needs in plain language, which the agents then interpret and act upon. Machine learning techniques may also be embedded to allow agents to learn from past projects, improving their performance and adaptability over time. This collaborative, modular, and fault-tolerant approach significantly reduces development time and errors while increasing scalability and accessibility. A prototype implementation demonstrates the feasibility of this model, showing substantial improvements over traditional methods in terms of speed, quality, and user experience. Overall, this research illustrates how multiagent interaction can revolutionize web development by making it faster, more intelligent, and accessible to a broader range of users, ultimately democratizing the creation of digital platforms across industries.

title: Train in Vain: Functionality-Preserving Poisoning to Prevent Unauthorized Use of Code Datasets
abstract: The widespread availability of large-scale code datasets has accelerated the development of code large language models (CodeLLMs), raising concerns about unauthorized dataset usage. Dataset poisoning offers a proactive defense by reducing the utility of such unauthorized training. However, existing poisoning methods often require full dataset poisoning and introduce transformations that break code compilability. In this paper, we introduce FunPoison, a functionality-preserving poisoning approach that injects short, compilable weak-use fragments into executed code paths. FunPoison leverages reusable statement-level templates with automatic repair and conservative safety checking to ensure side-effect freedom, while a type-aware synthesis module suppresses static analysis warnings and enhances stealth. Extensive experiments show that FunPoison achieves effective poisoning by contaminating only 10% of the dataset, while maintaining 100% compilability and functional correctness, and remains robust against various advanced code sanitization techniques.

title: Beyond Acoustic Sparsity and Linguistic Bias: A Prompt-Free Paradigm for Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis
abstract: Mispronunciation Detection and Diagnosis (MDD) requires modeling fine-grained acoustic deviations. However, current ASR-derived MDD systems often face inherent limitations. In particular, CTC-based models favor sequence-level alignments that neglect transient mispronunciation cues, while explicit canonical priors bias predictions toward intended targets. To address these bottlenecks, we propose a prompt-free framework decoupling acoustic fidelity from canonical guidance. First, we introduce CROTTC, an acoustic model enforcing monotonic, frame-level alignment to accurately capture pronunciation deviations. Second, we implicitly inject mispronunciation information via the IF strategy under the knowledge transfer principle. Experiments show CROTTC-IF achieves a 71.77% F1-score on L2-ARCTIC and 71.70% F1-score on the Iqra'Eval2 leaderboard. With empirical analysis, we demonstrate that decoupling acoustics from explicit priors provides highly robust MDD.
